PullRequest.Title: Add experiment-controlled runtime execution subagent settings
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Add separate settings for the execution subagent implemented in the Copilot runtime, rather than the extension-native execution subagent:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.enabled` | `false` |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.model` | `"gpt-5.6-luna"` |

Both settings are application-scoped and support startup experimentation treatments through `config.<setting ID>`. An explicitly empty model inherits the parent session model.

Reference: microsoft/vscode#340214 for the existing Agent Host experimentation plumbing. No tracking issue was provided.

## Behavior

Forward the settings into Agent Host root configuration and provide them as runtime ExP environment defaults. Runtime-fetched experiment assignments retain precedence over both values; inherited direct model overrides are stripped so they cannot bypass that precedence.

Both values participate in the existing safe runtime restart mechanism, which waits for all in-flight turns and subagents sharing the client to finish. Record setting-experiment exposure on parent turns, deferring telemetry until the forwarded assignment context arrives.

During session creation or resume, if the runtime's built-in catalog reports `execution_subagent`, remove the competing forwarded extension-native `executionSubagent` registration from that session. Preserve other tools and leave ordinary extension-backed Chat unchanged. Clarify the distinction in setting descriptions.

This PR does not change extension-native setting defaults or the `copilot-agent-runtime` repository.

## How to test manually

With no overriding runtime experiment assignment, enable `chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.enabled` and start a local Copilot Agent Host conversation. Confirm the runtime execution tool is offered with the default model. Select another available model, or explicitly set the model to `""` to inherit the parent model.

Change either setting during an active turn and confirm the turn and its subagents finish before the runtime is replaced. With the extension-native tool enabled, confirm only its forwarded registration is removed when the runtime catalog advertises the runtime implementation; unrelated client tools and ordinary extension-backed Chat should remain unaffected.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path, one-request-per-launch behavior, subprocess RPC boundary, and first-turn blocking are directly established by production code and the new create/resume tests. Only the exact duration and affected-cohort size are uncertain, which is reflected in low severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One runtime-subprocess RPC per affected session launch, plus a second full client-tool update when the runtime implementation is present
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost repeats once for every created or resumed Agent Host session whose snapshot contains the extension-native execution tool; concurrent launches each issue their own uncached request, and the optional setTools payload grows with the session's client-tool catalog.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased first-turn and resume latency from an additional serialized IPC round trip (and, when available, a second tool-catalog transmission) before the session can be handed to the turn.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: After createSession/resumeSession, finalization completed script safety, sandbox, and connector reconciliation without querying the runtime tool catalog or retransmitting client tools for this feature.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every launch containing `executionSubagent` now awaits `session.rpc.tools.getBuiltinDescriptors` after all other finalization work, and may then await `setTools`, before returning the wrapper.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 852 inserts `await this._configureExecutionSubagentTool(raw, config)` into `_finalizeSession`; the newly added helper at lines 866-875 performs the runtime RPC and optional `setTools`.
Findings.Title: Overlap the tool-catalog RPC with session finalization
Findings.Impact: For users with the extension-native execution-subagent treatment enabled, the first prompt in each new chat and the first prompt after a persisted chat is resumed wait for this extra subprocess round trip. The same work is repeated for every session, including when the runtime execution subagent is unavailable.
Findings.Evidence: `CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession` awaits `_sessionLauncher.launch` before registering the session, and both create and resume flow through `_finalizeSession`. The added line 852 awaits `_configureExecutionSubagentTool`; that helper unconditionally calls `session.rpc.tools.getBuiltinDescriptors({})` whenever `config.tools` contains `executionSubagent`, with no cache or coalescing. The added tests explicitly expect one descriptor request for every create/resume and for both runtime-default arms, confirming the multiplicity. The request is placed after the already-serialized script-safety, sandbox, and connector awaits, so none of its latency is overlapped.
Findings.Recommendation: Start the descriptor request as soon as the raw session is available and await it only before returning, so it overlaps independent script-safety/sandbox/connector work. If catalog availability is stable for a client, additionally coalesce/cache it per runtime (and model where inheritance makes availability model-dependent), invalidating on client restart.

Scenarios.Scenario: First prompt materializes a new local Copilot Agent Host chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The send queue awaits `_materializeProvisional`, which acquires/starts the Copilot runtime, builds a client-tool snapshot, calls `CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession`, and awaits launcher create/finalization before `entry.send` can begin. The added descriptor lookup and optional tool update are therefore on the first-response critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or reuse the Copilot runtime process and create the SDK session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one runtime startup per resident client and one createSession call per materialized chat; concurrent client acquisition is coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runtime acquisition and createSession boundary existed before the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply script-safety and sandbox session options; optionally reconcile connectors
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One options update and one sandbox application per created session; connector RPC/network work only when connectors are enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These finalization boundaries already ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized session-finalization work before the session is returned; pre-existing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query built-in tool descriptors from the runtime subprocess
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached request per created session whose client-tool snapshot contains `executionSubagent`, regardless of whether the runtime implementation is available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No runtime tool-catalog request was made on this launch path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly serialized after all preceding finalization and blocks first turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace the session's client tools with the extension execution tool filtered out
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional update per affected session when the runtime catalog contains `execution_subagent`; payload scales with all client tools in the session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Client tools were sent in the create configuration and were not retransmitted for this feature.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks session handoff after the descriptor request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of new chats materialized while the extension-native execution tool is registered; each chat contributes one descriptor RPC, and the optional tool-update serialization scales with the number and schema size of registered client tools.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A given chat is sequenced by its turn/session lifetime. Different chats may materialize concurrently; there is no cache, coalescer, or shared limiter for descriptor requests, so aggregate calls equal affected concurrent sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runtime client startup is shared/coalesced, but built-in descriptors are not cached or coalesced. Cold and warm session launches both issue the new request. No negative cache exists when the runtime execution tool is absent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: production call flow and added tests establish one awaited RPC for every affected create and both runtime availability arms.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact subprocess round-trip duration and treatment population are not measured; the extension-native tool defaults off but can be enabled explicitly or by experiment.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity latency regression because a new uncached IPC boundary is serialized on every affected first-turn launch and can be overlapped with independent finalization.

Scenarios.Scenario: First prompt resumes a persisted Agent Host chat that is not resident
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The send path awaits `_doResumeSession`, snapshot creation, SDK `resumeSession`, and `initializeSession`; both successful resume and empty-history fallback create flow through `_finalizeSession`, so the added tool-catalog request must finish before the resumed session can send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted session metadata and runtime session history/metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata read and one SDK resume per non-resident chat; fallback create occurs only for an empty-history resume error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Persisted chats already paid metadata and resume costs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query built-in descriptors and optionally resend filtered client tools
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One descriptor request per affected resume attempt that reaches finalization; one setTools update only when runtime execution is present. Empty-history fallback finalizes only the successful created session after failed resume.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Resume finalization did not query built-ins or resend tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds serialized latency before initializeSession continues to event-log registration and the turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of persisted chats resumed after eviction, restart, or window restoration while the extension execution tool is registered.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each session lifetime coalesces duplicate resumes for the same session; distinct sessions can resume concurrently and each performs its own descriptor request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No descriptor cache is shared across resumed sessions or across cold/warm runtime state; runtime client acquisition itself remains coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: resume and fallback paths visibly converge on the changed finalizer, and tests assert one request for resume.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resume frequency and RPC duration vary by user workflow; exact timings are not available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same reportable mechanism as the create scenario; included in the single finding rather than duplicated.

Scenarios.Scenario: User or startup experiment changes runtime execution-subagent enablement/model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench forwards changed settings through root-config protocol actions. Agent Host compares startup-baked configuration, waits for all active turns/subagents, disposes sessions and stops the runtime, then starts a new subprocess lazily on the next operation with updated environment defaults.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward each setting as a RootConfigChanged action to Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action per changed setting; initial forwarding is suppressed when root state already has the same structural value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two setting actions did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the active-turn critical path; it schedules restart handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop the Copilot runtime and lazily start a replacement with new ExP environment defaults
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Startup changes are folded into the current config; pending reasons are held while work is active, and no restart runs without an existing/starting client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changes to these nonexistent settings could not restart the runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Never interrupts active work; the next session use can pay cold-start/resume cost after the intentional setting change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit setting or startup-treatment changes, not number of turns or sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Restart waits for zero in-flight chats/subagents; startup acquisition is coalesced, and additional config events during stopping do not create parallel runtime processes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The replacement runtime is cold; resident session state must be resumed. Structural equality suppresses unchanged forwarded values.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the restart mechanism; low concern because it is bounded, deferred, and necessary for subprocess environment changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime startup duration varies, but these changes are infrequent and explicitly documented as requiring restart.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the expensive restart is intentional, safely deferred/coalesced, and triggered only by setting changes rather than a hot path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Parent SDK turn starts and records execution-setting experiment exposure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The `assistant.turn_start` event updates local turn state and invokes experiment-trigger telemetry for one enablement ID and, when enabled, one model ID. If assignment context is absent, IDs are held until a root-config event and flushed in a microtask.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Record experiment-trigger telemetry through the telemetry service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two setting IDs per parent turn call; child turns are skipped, and the telemetry helper/service deduplicates repeated exposure as covered by tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only HydraFusion exposure used the prior single pending boolean.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous local bookkeeping only; actual telemetry transport is outside this changed call path and not awaited by the turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of parent turn-start events. Pending cardinality is bounded by the fixed setting IDs, not session lifetime or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event handling is synchronous; deferred flush uses one microtask per qualifying root-config notification and a bounded Set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The Set deduplicates pending IDs until assignment context arrives and deletes each ID when logged; no unbounded retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that changed work is constant and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry implementation details are outside the changed code, but no awaited network/IPC boundary is introduced here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: constant-size local telemetry bookkeeping does not establish a concrete performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and all diff pages. One low-severity finding was submitted for the uncached runtime tool-catalog RPC newly serialized into every affected create/resume critical path. Restart, telemetry, environment construction, and pending-trigger lifecycle were bounded or intentionally deferred and did not warrant additional findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
